title: Esther before Ahasuerus
creator: Artemisia Gentileschi
description: A dramatic painted interpretation of Esther approaching the Persian king. Notice how gesture and the spacing of the figures convey the danger of the encounter.
caution: The museum describes a theatrical interpretation, not a reconstruction of the Persian court. Artistic details should not be read back into Scripture.

passages.note: An interpretation of Esther approaching the king; the painting adds dramatic details.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Gift of Elinor Dorrance Ingersoll, 1969.

title: The Hundred Guilder Print
creator: Rembrandt (Rembrandt van Rijn)
description: Rembrandt brings several episodes from Matthew 19 into one composition. Look at how light and the gathered figures direct attention toward Christ.
caution: A composite interpretation of a chapter, not a picture of one documented moment.

passages.note: The museum identifies several episodes from Matthew 19 combined in one scene.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. H. O. Havemeyer Collection, Bequest of Mrs. H. O. Havemeyer, 1929.

title: Adam and Eve
creator: Albrecht Dürer
description: An engraved interpretation of the first humans, set among closely observed animals and vegetation. Fine lines distinguish skin, fur and bark.
caution: Includes artistic nudity and later symbolism. It is a Renaissance interpretation, not a literal reconstruction of Eden.

passages.note: An artistic treatment of Adam and Eve and the forbidden fruit.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Fletcher Fund, 1919.

title: The Adoration of the Magi
creator: Giotto di Bondone
description: A gold-ground panel presenting the visit of the Magi. Notice the gestures around the child and the architectural framing of the scene.
caution: The dating is uncertain. Clothing, setting and gestures are artistic interpretation, not eyewitness evidence.

passages.note: An interpretation of the visit and homage of the Magi.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. John Stewart Kennedy Fund, 1911.

alt: The Adoration of the Magi — Giotto di Bondone

title: Sealed clay case for a legal tablet
creator: Maker unidentified
culture: Old Assyrian Trading Colony; probably Kültepe
description: A clay envelope impressed with cylinder seals, associated with a record of a lawsuit. It offers a tangible example of ancient legal documentation.
caution: A comparison from a different setting, not Abraham’s document and not evidence identifying the transaction in Genesis 23.

passages.note: Compare the idea of a witnessed transaction with surviving ancient legal records; this object is not connected to Abraham.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Gift of Mr. and Mrs. J. J. Klejman, 1966.

alt: Ancient clay tablet case with writing and seal impressions

title: Sickle sword
creator: Maker unidentified
description: An ancient curved bronze sword. Its shape offers a concrete comparison when reading imagery about weapons and peace.
caution: This object predates Isaiah by centuries. It is not a weapon from an event described in Isaiah, and its form does not establish how it was used.

passages.note: A comparison for the imagery of swords, not an object from Isaiah’s lifetime.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Gift of J. Pierpont Morgan, 1911.

title: Glass ribbed bowl
creator: Maker unidentified
description: A surviving ribbed glass bowl from the early Roman imperial world. Notice its material, shallow profile and repeated ribs.
caution: A period comparison for daily-life vessels, not a vessel owned or used by Jesus or his followers.

passages.note: A material-culture comparison alongside references to washing vessels.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Gift of Henry G. Marquand, 1881.

title: Head of Augustus
creator: Maker unidentified
description: A surviving small portrait head of Augustus, the ruler named at the opening of Luke 2. The object makes the imperial setting more tangible.
caution: An imperial portrait, not evidence for a particular census or the circumstances of Jesus’ birth. The object’s date and origin follow the museum record.

passages.note: Augustus is named in Luke 2:1; this portrait supplies imperial context.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Gift of Edward S. Harkness, 1926.

alt: Ancient faience portrait head of Augustus

title: Glass gold-band perfume bottle
creator: Maker unidentified
description: A slender ancient perfume container with gold-band decoration. It shows one of the designs used for storing fragrant substances.
caution: This is a glass alabastron, not alabaster. It is not the vessel in Luke 7 and should not be presented as an exact illustration of that object.

passages.note: A comparison for perfume containers, distinct from the alabaster vessel named in this passage.

source.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
source.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Gift of J. Pierpont Morgan, 1917.

alt: Ancient glass perfume bottle with gold-band decoration

title: Ethiopian Gospel-book leaf: the entombment of Christ
creator: Ethiopian artist unidentified
description: The recto of a surviving illustrated Gospel-book leaf shows Joseph and Nicodemus carrying Christ toward the tomb.
caution: A medieval manuscript illustration, not an original first-century Gospel manuscript. Its visual traditions are distinct from the wording of the passage.

passages.note: A later Ethiopian visual interpretation of the burial of Christ.

source.name: The Walters Art Museum
source.credit: The Walters Art Museum. Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Joseph Knopfelmacher, 1996.

alt: Ethiopian Gospel-book leaf showing the entombment of Christ

title: The Sea of Galilee and its surrounding fields
creator: Davidi Vardi
description: A present-day view across agricultural land toward the Sea of Galilee. It helps establish the relationship between the lake and surrounding terrain.
caution: A modern landscape, including modern agriculture and settlements, not a reconstruction of the first century.

passages.note: The lake setting helps visualize the calling of fishermen.
Geographic context for a crossing of the lake.
Geographic context for fishing on the lake.
Geographic context for the Sea of Tiberias.

alt: Modern fields and settlements beside the Sea of Galilee

title: Acts: a narrative journey
creator: YourBible
description: A selective reading guide through several settings in Acts, from Jerusalem to Rome. The sequence follows the narrative rather than attempting to date every event.
caution: Not a travel map, complete chronology or archaeological object. The diagram deliberately omits disputed calendar dates.

passages.note: A selective overview of the book’s narrative settings.

source.name: YourBible
source.credit: YourBible. Original study diagram; Scripture references supplied for comparison.
